atlas-cn.0155: The national civil-service exam alone offered 38,100 central posts for 2026, and the four big state banks plan about 64,000 graduate hires. State-owned firms are a core graduate employer.
atlas-cn.0156: The ordinary Category B work permit asks for a degree plus two years of experience, or 60 points; only the 2017 graduate route lets a fresh master’s graduate in, and the employer must file for it. Few entry roles are offered to foreigners; the rules themselves are under Visas.
atlas-cn.0157: A photo is common on Chinese-language CVs, though a UK careers service says it depends on the role. Age and hometown often appear too.
atlas-cn.0158: Keep the CV to one or two pages, tailored to the role. Most graduate roles also need an application form on top of the CV, and personal statements are not usual.
atlas-cn.0159: Personal statements are not usual; where one is wanted, a cover letter should be one page and tailored to the role.
atlas-cn.0160: References are not part of the first application; employers check previous schools and employers at offer stage. No page we read describes this, so treat it as our reading.
atlas-cn.0161: Chinese employers often require the degree certificate before signing a formal employment contract. For a work permit, foreign diplomas need an apostille, which replaced consular legalisation between Italy and China on 7 November 2023.
atlas-cn.0162: For experienced hires pay is negotiated at offer: job changers typically expect a 10% to 20% rise and bonuses are common. Graduate programmes set their own pay scale, which is rarely negotiated (our reading).
atlas-cn.0163: Reference and background checks are made by some employers, mostly multinationals and state firms, before an offer is final. No page we read states how routine this is.
atlas-cn.0164: Campaigns and platforms take applications, but personal referrals and face-to-face networking remain powerful, and guanxi can decide hiring in state-owned and smaller firms.
atlas-cn.0165: A foreigner without a Chinese or well-known foreign master’s needs a degree and two years of experience, or 60 points, and an employer who files for the permit. Overseas graduates can use Chinese campus recruitment for two years after graduating.
atlas-cn.0166: CVs for local employment should be in Chinese; bilingual CVs are recommended for joint ventures, wholly foreign-owned firms and multinationals. English counts as an asset mainly for international or overseas-facing roles.
atlas-cn.0167: State-owned companies use aptitude tests and HR-led interviews; joint ventures and multinationals run processes closer to Western ones. Assessment centres are less common than in the UK but growing, with group discussions and case studies the usual exercises.
atlas-cn.0168: Students describe the autumn drive as a run of civil-service-style aptitude tests (xíngcè), written tests (bǐshì) and large group interviews. Most graduate roles need an application form as well as a CV, and many Chinese selection tests are essay-based.
atlas-cn.0169: Offers cluster in November and December for the autumn drive. Huawei publishes a video on the interview process for its R&D campus roles.
atlas-cn.0170: Interviews are formal: a handshake and the surname first, and personal questions are more common than in some Western interviews. Close by asking when a decision will be communicated.
atlas-cn.0171: The civil-service route is a nationwide written test, held on 30 November for the 2026 exam, followed by an eligibility review and an interview.
atlas-cn.0172: Probation is capped by the contract term: none under three months, one month for three months to under a year, two months for one to under three years, six months for three years or more. An employer can impose it only once.
atlas-cn.0173: During probation pay may not fall below 80% of the agreed salary or the local minimum wage. An employee can resign on 3 days’ written notice, against 30 days once confirmed.
atlas-cn.0174: Contracts are fixed-term or open-ended; if a written contract is not signed within a year of starting, the arrangement counts as open-ended. Employers often want the degree certificate before signing.
atlas-cn.0175: A notice period of about one month is typical for experienced hires, who negotiate: job changers expect a 10% to 20% rise, bonuses are common, and a counteroffer from the current employer is likely.
atlas-cn.0176: Fresh graduates on campus schemes get a fixed offer on the employer’s own scale and rarely negotiate (our reading).
atlas-cn.0177: For a fresh foreign graduate the door is the 2017 notice: a master’s or above from a Chinese or well-known overseas university, within one year of graduating, an average grade of at least 80 of 100 (or B+/B), a definite employer, and a job in the field paid at least the local average urban wage.
atlas-cn.0178: Otherwise the ordinary Category B permit asks for a degree and two years of post-graduation experience, or at least 60 points on the SAFEA scheme (degree, age, salary, Chinese-language level, location). The employer files the application before the visa, so the offer comes first.
atlas-cn.0179: What an employer needs to hear: the role fits the degree, the salary clears the local average, and you will not start work before the residence permit is issued. Ask early whether it has filed for a foreign graduate before.
atlas-cn.0180: The Ministry of Education’s National College Student Employment Service Platform (ncss.cn) lists graduate jobs, including state-owned firms, public institutions and internships, runs employer events and links to provincial and school sites.
atlas-cn.0181: Zhaopin, Liepin, 51job and BOSS Zhipin cover all levels; Shixiseng is the internship and campus board; HiredChina serves international talent; EOL, Yingjiesheng and Job1001 list graduate vacancies; GradLink China serves UK-educated Chinese students.
atlas-cn.0182: WeChat official accounts and group chats, and Xiaohongshu posts about campus recruiting, are where much recruiting news and informal coffee chats travel.
atlas-cn.0183: Huawei’s campus portal lists its graduate and internship drives, an Open Day and online talks, and warns of fake internship referrals and recommendation letters circulating online (notice of 11 May 2026).
atlas-cn.0184: Starting in November. The early tech batch opens in June or July, the main drive from September, and most offers are out by December.
atlas-cn.0185: Sending an English-only CV to a local employer. CVs for local employment should be in Chinese; bilingual CVs suit multinationals, joint ventures and wholly foreign-owned firms.
atlas-cn.0186: Finishing a one-year master’s in winter and expecting a summer start: the degree certificate is often needed before the contract is signed.
atlas-cn.0187: Treating the 30-day visa-free entry as permission to work or intern, or starting an internship on a study visa without the school’s consent and a note on the permit.
atlas-cn.0188: Paying or trusting an online “referral” for an internship: Huawei itself has warned of fake internship referrals and recommendation letters.
atlas-cn.0189: Banks recruit through Chinese-language campus campaigns, and CVs for local employment should be in Chinese. No page we read states a level; treat advanced Mandarin as the working assumption.
atlas-cn.0190: Multinationals and joint ventures, the Big Four among them, are where bilingual CVs are recommended and English is an asset.
atlas-cn.0191: The big tech campaigns and Huawei’s campus portal are in Chinese. English is valued mainly for global-facing roles at companies going overseas.
atlas-cn.0192: Banks such as China Merchants Bank recruit AI researchers who know banking through the usual Chinese campus channels, where CVs for local employment should be in Chinese. No page we read states a level for these roles.
atlas-cn.0193: X1 study visa and residence permit
atlas-cn.0194: For courses over 180 days: with the admission notice and the JW201 or JW202 form, an X1 visa valid 30 days from arrival; within 30 days, the health check and a residence permit for study. Up to 180 days, an X2 visa with no residence permit.
atlas-cn.0195: From the second year, students may intern up to 8 hours a week in term, only after the police add an “internship” note to the residence permit.
atlas-cn.0198: visa €45 + €67.10 centre; insurance 800 RMB; permit 800 RMB
atlas-cn.0199: There is no general internship visa. Students of foreign universities can intern only through government agreements or pilot schemes in free-trade zones, on an S2 visa noted “internship”. Graduates cannot: a “post-graduate internship” on a tourist or business visa is illegal work.
atlas-cn.0201: There is no job-search visa. A master’s or PhD from a Chinese university or a world top-500 university, with grades of at least 80/100, waives the two years of experience if you apply within a year of graduating, for a job paying at least the local average wage.
atlas-cn.0204: Z work visa and residence permit
atlas-cn.0205: The employer obtains a work-permit notification online; you need a degree and two years of experience, or 60 points. The Z visa is valid 30 days: register your address within 24 hours, then convert to a residence permit within 30 days.
atlas-cn.0206: High-end talent (85 points, or six times the local average wage) gets a free R visa of 5 or 10 years; a new K visa lets young STEM graduates enter without an employer.
atlas-cn.0208: Miss the 30-day deadline and you are staying illegally: 500 RMB a day, detention and expulsion.
